adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in useAllRulerRuleAbilities (lines 240-275), the code now hardcodes 'const isFederated = false;' with a TODO comment 'Add support for federated rules'. The previous implementation in useAllAlertRuleAbilities called 'isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)' to check if a rule group was federated. Since useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities via 'return useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)', all existing consumers that relied on federated rule detection will now incorrectly treat federated Mimir groups as mutable (allowing Update/Delete operations). This is a real behavioral regression - federated rules should be immutable but will now be treated as editable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at line 172 and the AlertRuleMenu component, the canDelete permission check is used to determine whether to SHOW the delete menu option, not to execute deletion. The actual deletion would happen through a separate action handler that would use the rulerRule. The OR logic is intentional - it allows the menu to show when EITHER the ruler-based check OR the grafana-prom-based check passes. This is designed for the list view case where rulerRule may be undefined (skipToken is passed). When rulerRule exists, its permissions are checked; when only promRule exists, those permissions are checked. The finding incorrectly claims this creates a security issue where provisioned rules could be deleted, but the deletion action itself would still need to go through proper authorization. The comment in the code explicitly explains this dual-check pattern is for the list view optimization.
